contributions.statement: When a repo's agent workflow is compiled from a Markdown prompt file that lives in another repo, treat that file as a versioned dependency: pin the source commit and, before recompiling, diff its frontmatter (permissions, tools, triggers, safe-outputs, network) explicitly rather than trusting file size, because shared sources keep changing and most edits land in execution settings rather than instructions.
contributions.evidence: §III-B/§V-A: 108 of 365 gh-aw projects (29.6%) reference Markdown from another repository. §IV-B Finding #4: project-median 74.5% of maintenance changes touch frontmatter vs 50.0% body (pooled 62.1% vs 55.1%; frontmatter-only share 36.7% -> 71.7% from month 1 to 4). §V-A: one-third of content-changing events leave line count unchanged. Descriptive mining of 348 files in 43 repos selected for >=120-day spans (audit); no breakage or incident outcome is measured.
relative_to: pin third-party GitHub Actions / reusable workflows to a commit SHA (known supply-chain practice)
2607.03691 pin agent-host versions and re-probe before upgrade

contributions.statement: Put firm limits (comment counts, write targets, tool access) in the workflow's enforced configuration and use the prompt body only to explain them, keeping the two consistent when either changes.
contributions.evidence: §V-A(3): dotnet/aspnetcore example where the body says 'post at most one comment' and frontmatter sets safe-outputs add-comment max: 1. One illustrative case; prevalence of duplicated or conflicting rules is not measured.
relative_to: 2608.23550 treat prose security rules as unenforced; compile them into host controls

reason: A descriptive mining study with no outcome data, but its cross-repo reuse rate and frontmatter-dominated churn give a specific review target for teams sharing agent workflow sources across repos; the enforcement-vs-prose advice is already in the KB.
